name: Koombiyo Delivery
author: itdp7788

sections.description:
Koombiyo Delivery connects your WooCommerce store to the Koombiyo Delivery courier network (Sri Lanka): assign waybills and dispatch orders in bulk, track shipment status and Proof of Delivery, and request courier pickups — all from your WordPress admin.

The plugin works as a standalone WooCommerce extension (one site-level Koombiyo account), or in multi-vendor mode with WCFM or Dokan, where each vendor connects and uses their own independent Koombiyo merchant account.

Requires

  • WooCommerce (required)
  • WCFM Marketplace or Dokan (optional — enables multi-vendor mode; neither is required for standalone use)
  • A Koombiyo Delivery merchant account (contact Koombiyo Delivery to obtain API credentials)

External services

This plugin connects to the Koombiyo Delivery courier service, provided by Koombiyo Delivery (Pvt) Ltd in Sri Lanka. A Koombiyo Delivery account is required. Nothing is sent until a store owner or vendor connects their account.

Koombiyo Delivery API (https://client.koombiyodelivery.lk) is used to dispatch and track orders.

  • Your API key and password are sent when you connect an account, and when the plugin has to sign in again.
  • Customer name, phone numbers, delivery address, city and postal code, order number, order description, cash on delivery amount, product value and your notes are sent when you dispatch an order.
  • A waybill number is sent when you open shipment details, a timeline or a Proof of Delivery, print waybills or delete a shipment.
  • Pickup address, phone number, map location, quantity, remark and vehicle type are sent when you request a pickup.
  • Your account login token is sent with these requests and when the plugin loads the Dashboard, the notices banner, active waybills or the order and pickup lists.
  • A waybill or pickup is looked up when Koombiyo sends this site a status update, so the plugin can confirm the update before changing anything. If delivery updates are off on a single-vendor account, no lookup is made.

Koombiyo notice images: a notice from Koombiyo may include an image, which your browser then loads from the address Koombiyo gave, on the plugin’s admin pages.

Koombiyo tracking page (https://koombiyodelivery.lk): the “Order dispatched” customer email links to Koombiyo’s tracking page. When a customer opens the link, the waybill number and phone number in it are sent to Koombiyo.

Status updates from Koombiyo: Koombiyo sends status updates to this site’s REST API addresses shown under API Settings, once you save them in the Koombiyo portal. They contain a waybill or pickup ID and its status.

Koombiyo Delivery terms of service: https://koombiyodelivery.lk/about (select “Terms & Conditions” at the bottom of the page)
Koombiyo Delivery privacy policy: https://koombiyodelivery.lk/privacy_policy

OpenStreetMap is used for the map where you choose a pickup location on the Pickup Requests screen. While that map is showing, your browser loads map images from OpenStreetMap’s servers (https://tile.openstreetmap.org), which receive your IP address and the map area being viewed. No order or customer details are sent. The service is provided by the OpenStreetMap Foundation.

OpenStreetMap terms of use: https://osmfoundation.org/wiki/Terms_of_Use
OpenStreetMap tile usage policy: https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/tiles/
OpenStreetMap privacy policy: https://osmfoundation.org/wiki/Privacy_Policy

Source code

The human-readable source of the compiled JavaScript and CSS in build/ is included in this plugin, in the src/ folder, with package.json and webpack.config.js.

To rebuild it, run npm install and then npm run build in the plugin folder. This needs Node.js and uses @wordpress/scripts.

The Pickup Requests map uses Leaflet 1.9.4 (BSD-2-Clause license), which is bundled into build/, along with its marker images. Its source is at https://github.com/Leaflet/Leaflet.
sections.changelog:
1.1.3

  • Tested with WordPress 7.2 and WooCommerce 11.3.
  • Ship Orders: orders are given the lowest free waybills first, with the highest of those on the newest order.
  • Ship Orders: click the Order No heading to show the newest or the oldest orders first.
  • Ship Orders: pages with Prev/Next and 20, 50 or 100 orders per page, so orders beyond the first 20 can be reached.
  • Ship Orders: a Columns button to hide columns you don’t need.
  • Fixed: the Ship Orders search found nothing on stores that do not use WooCommerce’s order tables (HPOS). It now finds orders by number, name, email, phone, address or city.

1.1.2

  • Security: a status update sent to this site is now confirmed with Koombiyo before anything changes, and the reply no longer shows any order details.
  • WooCommerce order list: a new Koombiyo column shows “Not dispatched”, or the waybill and latest delivery status. Dokan parent orders show how many sub-orders are dispatched.
  • The “Order dispatched” email now links to Koombiyo’s current tracking page.
  • Track Orders: the timeline always shows the latest status first, and each phone number stays on one line.
  • Ship Orders, Track Orders and Pickup Requests: tables fit the screen, so the sideways scrollbar is always in reach.
  • Admin scripts now load as files through WordPress, and the WordPress.org download no longer includes Word copies of the guides.
  • Dispatching no longer marks an order Completed. It stays Processing until Koombiyo reports Delivered, or until you complete it yourself.
  • Only Koombiyo’s Delivered status completes an order.
  • New “Order dispatched” customer email with the waybill number and a tracking link (single-vendor accounts). Manage it under WooCommerce > Settings > Emails.
  • Ship Orders: add an optional second phone number with the + button.
  • Phone numbers must now be 0 followed by 9 digits before an order can be dispatched.
  • Phone numbers display as 077-123 4567 on Ship Orders and Track Orders.
  • Active waybills load highest number first, to match the newest-first order list.

1.1.1

  • Replaces the earlier Koombiyo Delivery plugin (v1.1.x): orders it already shipped are not offered for shipping again, and can be imported with their waybills.
  • Cash on delivery vs prepaid payments: each payment method is detected as COD or prepaid, with an override per method.
  • Koombiyo notices and alerts are shown as a banner on the plugin pages.
  • Optional “Delivered” updates from Koombiyo for single-store accounts.
  • Webhook URLs no longer contain the API key. Clients who saved the old URL in the Koombiyo portal must save the new one.

0.1.0

  • First public release.
  • Full admin UI: Dashboard, Ship Orders (bulk dispatch with auto-assigned waybills), Track Orders (filters, column chooser, print formats, live timeline), Pickup Requests (map-based location picker).
  • Full Koombiyo API client, dispatch/tracking business logic, multi-row dispatch audit log, HPOS compatibility.
  • GDPR-style personal data export/erase, and an uninstall data-retention setting.

Internal development milestone (pre-release)

  • Initial repository scaffold (Phase 1: directory structure, autoloader, plugin bootstrap, dev tooling). No functional features yet.
  • Phase 2: WooCommerce dependency check (blocks activation, and goes inert with a notice if WooCommerce is deactivated later), Store_Context/Context_Resolver tenancy detection for standalone WooCommerce / WCFM / Dokan (including the fail-closed both-active-and-unresolved case), capability + default-option registration on activation. No admin screens, credential storage, or Koombiyo API calls yet.
  • Phase 3: API Settings page (native admin UI) to connect/disconnect a Koombiyo Delivery account; encrypted (AES-256-GCM) credential storage in a new wp_koombiyo_clients table; a minimal Koombiyo_Client seed (login/logout only — full API surface arrives in Phase 4).
